WriteToolsGuides

Small things in October

See the month as scenes Open the demo in Writer Open the protected copy

A fictional journal for 1–31 October 2026, with one entry and one saved 3D scene for every day. Names, experiences, measurements and recordings are demonstration material. Nothing here describes a real person's journal.

Open demo-month.jotz in Write → Open. It carries the writing and attached files together, including the saved scenes. Reading it does not need an AI connection or a provider account. Prepare Writer for offline use once, then the saved journal can be opened without a connection. External media references remain links; the songs, films and books they name are not downloaded.

The readable authoring source is demo-month.jot. Open the .jotz for the complete demonstration: the source file alone does not carry its pictures, recordings, models or scenes.

Both archives include stable entry identities, archive metadata and a portable public SQLite search index. This demo explicitly includes that index even though its writing is below the normal 256 KiB threshold. A normal Writer save may omit an unnecessary small-journal index; local search still reads the same source. Attachments retain their original bytes and readable names, while archive members use UUID identities.

Look around

  1. Open Scenes, choose a day and turn its place. Choose a named thing beside it to read the sentences it holds. Open journal shows the corresponding entry; Go to this entry returns to the writing. Try a rainy day and Pause motion, or use reduced motion in Writing preferences. See the month as scenes shows the same scenes on their own, without Writer.
  2. Open Map to follow the month, cross-entry links and tag threads. Choose an entry, then Open in writing.
  3. Open Media to browse the book, film, series, anime, podcast, game and music references. Compare a mention with an explicit activity such as Reading or Watched. Download media journal saves a separate writing-only copy.
  4. Choose Tools → Page preview to read the finished pages. Compare Typed styles with Handwritten, change paper, then try Page view, Download page, EPUB ↓ or Print / PDF. These page exports are unencrypted.
  5. Switch between Live editing and Source editing. Tick a task, edit a phrase, try Undo, and save a separate .jotz copy. Browser autosave and a downloaded or device-saved file are separate copies.

The scene-generation tool uses Writer's actual scene pipeline: journalDays extracts the day's prose, placePrompt numbers its sentences, requestJSON asks OpenRouter for scene data, and validatePlace replaces sentence numbers with the entry's exact words. Scratchpads, hidden comments, code and records are excluded. Model-returned text never replaces the journal's writing. Saved scenes live in demo-scenes/ and carry the model and generation time. All 31 saved scenes were generated through OpenRouter with openai/gpt-5-mini, with Zero Data Retention required and data collection denied. Each scene's object, shape and exact sentence-link counts, generation time and hashes are recorded in the provenance index.

Choose an object to see its saved sentences. Editing a sentence later leaves its saved scene unchanged, and Writer marks an old moment as no longer in the entry. To make a fresh scene with your own model, configure the AI companion for the session, then choose Make this day's scene and review what will be sent. A new scene is a draft until Keep it. Reading a saved scene makes no AI request.

Try protection

demo-month-mixed.jotz is a second copy for exploring public and protected entries. Its demo passphrase is jot-demo-only. It is public demonstration material; this published passphrase offers no privacy.

Open the mixed copy and choose Cancel in the unlock prompt to read the public entries while locked. The 31 October entry is protected. All attached files, saved scenes and archive settings are protected too, including attachments referenced by public entries. Unlock with the demo passphrase to explore the complete journal, then reload Writer, cancel the unlock prompt and try Search public entries. Private text is searchable only while unlocked, and never enters the portable public search index. Dates and encryption metadata remain visible.

In an unlocked copy, Tools → Entries, privacy and search lets you change which entries are public. Ways in lets you explore changing a passphrase, adding a recovery code, or enrolling a PRF-capable passkey where supported. Save a new copy after changing protection. Earlier copies keep their earlier settings. Keep a recovery code separately from the journal; real passkeys, password managers and recovery routes must be set up on your own device.

Tools to try on a copy

Some Writer features are actions or local preferences, rather than content a journal can contain.

Workflow Try it in Writer
Writing and navigation Find & replace, Outline, Tools search, Keyboard shortcuts, formatting, list continuation and Undo/Redo
Starting and continuing Entry templates, Today, Quick note, Carry tasks forward and Week review; time-sensitive actions use the current day, so they may add entries after October
Scratchpad and margin notes Open 26 October's scratchpad, select notes and Add to entry; add a margin note to any passage
Layout and preferences Focus mode, writing size/spacing/width, high contrast, reduced motion, return-to-position, handwriting, dots, paper and page styles
Files and exports Attached files → View / Download original; Save as, Download journal, plain Jot/Markdown exports, Calendar .ics, Numbers/Tasks .csv, standalone HTML, fixed-layout EPUB and print
Numbers and imports Import a fictional numbers CSV or a supported sample health export; review before adding. Your life online converts supported data exports separately
Drawing Annotate page; draw on a frozen page copy and reopen its editable strokes
Reference books Open a People or Places book explicitly, try local suggestions, then unload it; books are separate files and are not automatically copied into a journal
Connected context and media Review a weather or read-only Home Assistant snapshot; enable a catalog lookup or listening connection only if you want to contact that service
AI and voice Configure the optional AI companion, review a draft, or make a new scene; Scribe, voice typing and voice practice each require their own explicit microphone action and any model setup
Keeping and transferring Prepare offline use, request persistent storage, review an outgoing journal/excerpt, try system sharing or pair two devices for nearby transfer
Protection and recovery Use the mixed copy above; test reload, unlock, relock, public/private search and a separately saved archive

For the reference-book workflow, download people.jot and places.jot, then open them explicitly in People & Places. They match the links on 23 October and remain separate from the journal. For number import, use demo-numbers.csv, which contains fictional sample data.

Provider credentials, microphone recordings, speech-model weights, passkeys, browser preferences, file handles and device permissions are not embedded in this demo. No service is contacted merely by opening the journal. Browser and device support varies; an attached recording's codec, a PDF viewer, EPUB scripting and physical microphone/stylus behavior still depend on the reader.

Jot remains a prototype. The 62 method profiles are a catalog of optional record structures; this month demonstrates supported content and Writer workflows, rather than claiming 62 specialized clinical or method-specific applications. Diagram fences and unfamiliar records preserve readable source; a diagram engine or full custom-layout renderer is not supplied by putting that source in the journal. Planned features are not represented as working controls.

Rebuild the demo

Packaging reads the saved scenes and does not call a model:

node tools/build-demo-journal.mjs
node cli/jot.mjs check --strict examples/demo-month.jot examples/demo-month.jotz

To generate or refresh scenes, configure OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your environment, then run:

node tools/generate-demo-scenes.mjs
node tools/build-demo-journal.mjs

This explicit command sends each day's extracted prose to OpenRouter using the model selected with --model or OPENROUTER_MODEL (default openai/gpt-5-mini). Zero Data Retention is required by default and data collection is denied. It saves successful days as it goes; rerunning reuses only scenes whose model, privacy policy, prompt, sentences and saved bytes still match. The provenance index records those hashes and generation times without credentials. Missing credentials or failed requests stop generation; no substitute scenes or silent model/privacy fallback is used. Review generated places in Writer before publishing a rebuilt demo. Validation of the mixed archive also requires unlocking it; a syntax check of its locked public source cannot establish validity of protected entries.
